name: Africa Business and BYU Pathway Project
text:
Africa Business and BYU Pathway Project -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: BYU Pathway Consulting Project Element:.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 20 May–23 Jun | $6,000–6,400.
KENYA, BOTSWANA, ZIMBABWE, SOUTH AFRICA
Experience successful business models in Kenya, Botswana, Zimbabwe and South Africa, while working directly with BYU Pathway students to help build a successful business in South Africa. This will be your opportunity to develop your own skills in business while contributing to creating jobs for BYU Pathway students. This study abroad program is a hybrid between a regular study abroad program in international business and an international development consulting project. This program is available to students in all majors, both inside and outside of the Marriott School of Business.
BYU Pathway Consulting Project Element:
Student teams will spend two weeks in Johannesburg, South Africa, working with local and global business leaders, including the BYU Management Society, to help BYU Pathway Worldwide students start and improve their local business ventures. We are interested in students with a passion to learn from local businesses in Africa and apply those learnings to collaboratively identify customers and marketing needs, develop a business strategy, build financial and accounting models, identify sourcing and supply chain opportunities, and manage a local workforce. Before leaving for Africa, we will spend the second half of winter semester 2027 in a once-a-week evening class working with these BYU Pathway students online to prepare for our in-country experience. Students from a variety of backgrounds and majors will be needed for each team to work on diverse projects.
Study Abroad Program Element:
Successful business models in Africa will be studied and examined at the beginning of the trip, starting with a week in Nairobi, Kenya, known as the Silicon Savannah. Nairobi will offer us insight into the one of Africa’s top technology and startup hubs. Here we will also visit Mully Children’s Family (MCF), established by former Kenyan entrepreneur and millionaire Charles Mulli and his wife Esther to help care for thousands of street children. We will then fly to Botswana to see how one of the poorest countries transformed itself into one of the richest countries in Africa by investing in diamond discovery, strong governance, and careful financial management. We’ll also spend time in Cape Town, South Africa, the top hub for ease of doing business. Cape Town leads Africa in technology, finance, and corporate headquarters. It also provides an interesting cultural context for learning about Apartheid and the history of South Africa. We will finish the trip with a safari, a game drive, and a visit to Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe.

name: Ancient and Modern Worldbuilding
text:
Ancient and Modern Worldbuilding -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: ITALY, GREECE, EGYPT, FRANCE, UK.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 4 May–16 Jun | $8,800–9,200.
ITALY, GREECE, EGYPT, FRANCE, UK
STUDY ABROAD GENERAL EDUCATION (SAGE)
Why do men think about the Roman Empire so much? How have ancient civilizations, from Greece, Egypt, and Rome to the Anglo-Saxons and Druids, shaped the world we live in today? On this exciting program we will trace both the actual worlds built by ancient cultures and the way modern culture has rebuilt the ancient world in stories, plays, operas, paintings, and film. We’ll walk in the Romans’ footsteps from the Via Appia and Pompeii to Lutetia (Paris) and Londinium (London), visiting iconic landmarks, connecting with international artists, and growing spiritually, intellectually, and creatively. With faculty-led excursions and hands-on learning, you’ll leave with lifelong memories, meaningful friendships, and a global perspective—plus plenty of gelato and fresh baguettes! Enjoy Europe’s springtime, without the oppressive heat and crowds that fill the city and its museums later in the summer. We'll visit Rome, Florence, Volterra, Cairo, Luxor, Athens, Crete, Paris, and London.

name: Art & Language in France
text:
Art & Language in France -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: no prior French language experience is required.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 14 May–14 Jun | $5,400–5,900.
Fulfill GE requirements in London, Paris, and Marseille with an Art professor and a French professor! Through coursework and real-world interactions at museums and monuments of London, Paris, and southern France, we will explore how art and language shape identity.
Our first week will start in London with visits to the British Museum, the National Gallery, the Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration, and the Victoria and Albert Museum. We'll spend the next two weeks in Paris, learning about the artistic movements of Expressionism and Impressionism in the place where they originated. Museum visits to the Louvre, the Musée d'Orsay, and Monet's gardens in Giverny will be complemented by student art projects and experiences, including the opportunity to paint on-site in the gardens where Monet lived and worked. Students will learn foundational principles of linguistics as they get out into the city to learn and use essential French phrases in simple interactions. The final week of the program will take us to Marseille, where we will explore the art, language, and culture of the Mediterranean, including a visit to the city of Arles where Vincent Van Gogh created over 300 paintings.
Coursework includes an introduction to the French language; however,
no prior French language experience is required
.
Click here
to apply today!
Courses:
Students will enroll in two 3-credit classes (6 credit hours total) of the following courses while on this program:
UNIV 210—Intro to Linguistic Systems and Analysis
, 3 credit hours (fulfills GE requirements for Global and Cultural Awareness)
Explore French and English language systems, how language shapes intercultural communication, and how differences can lead to both misunderstanding and connection. Build practical French communication skills while developing greater empathy for those navigating new languages and cultures.
UNIV 214—Drawing and Composition
, 3 credit hours (fulfills GE requirements for Arts)
Experience France and London through art while developing your own creative voice. Create a travel sketchbook, explore artists and visual traditions, analyze art encountered at cultural sites, and develop skills in color, composition, and artistic expression through hands-on projects inspired by your experiences abroad.

name: International Biology Internships: Vanuatu
text:
International Biology Internships: Vanuatu -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Internship Win 2027 | 3 months during winter | $3,700–4,200.
A small cohort of students will live independently in Tanna, Vanuatu, a Pacific island archipelago, approximately 1,400 miles from Australia, 3,500 miles from Hawaii, and 4,200 miles from Japan, during winter semester. Students will conduct field research on this unique research-based internship. Vanuatu is famous for cultural diversity and tradition and is a rich biodiverse setting for a biology field internship. Students internship research will focus on the evolution of insects with a major focus on dragonflies and beetles. By collecting samples, students will learn about insect distribution and behavior. The internship is designed to not only provide a completely unique research experience but also to result in presentations at national meetings and publishing in peer-reviewed publications with student authors. The goal is to produce wing morphology data to explore the evolution of flight strategies over the evolutionary history of dragonflies, insect order Odonata.

name: Building Zion Beyond Borders: Western Canada
text:
Building Zion Beyond Borders: Western Canada -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 20 Jul–11 Aug (approx.) | $2,800–3,300.
Western Canada provides a distinctive setting for studying the ways gender, culture, religion, colonialism, and civic life shape people’s experiences of belonging. Through GWS 222, Introduction to Global Women’s Studies, and IAS 397R, Fostering Belonging, students will examine the contributions of women to Canadian politics, social reform, religion, the arts, environmental stewardship, and community building. Particular attention will be given to Indigenous women’s resilience and leadership, and contemporary efforts toward truth, reconciliation, and decolonization, and the experiences of early LDS women settlers. By learning in the places where these histories unfolded and from people whose communities continue to be shaped by them, students will explore how Christlike compassion, civic leadership, peacemaking, and covenant belonging can help create communities in which all people are valued.
The study abroad will begin in Calgary, Alberta, with travel through Banff, Lake Louise, Waterton, and surrounding communities before continuing to British Columbia and Vancouver Island, and ending in the city of Vancouver. Experiences will include visits to sites connected to the Famous Five and women’s political leadership, museums and historic locations examining pioneer life and social reform, and cultural and natural landscapes of multiple Canadian national parks. Program activities may include Indigenous-led cultural learning, Heritage Park, the Royal BC Museum, First Peoples cultural centers, and sites connected to Indigenous stewardship and reconciliation. Throughout the program, students will experience Canada’s remarkable history, cultures, cities, and natural landscapes while considering how women and marginalized communities have contributed to building more peaceful, inclusive, and equitable societies.

name: BYU London Centre Fall
text:
BYU London Centre Fall -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Fall 2027 | 31 Aug–6 Dec (approx.) | $13,800–14,300.
In
The Republic
, Plato famously used the metaphor of a city to seek to understand how the human soul can be good and just. During our fall 2027 program, we will provide a crash course in how to mold oneself into a good citizen and disciple. Our text will be London, its history, its physical layout and character, and its people. These hold many lessons pertaining to individual and community identity, the profit and perils of force, the vulnerability of oppressors, the power held by the oppressed, and how language can be a tool or a weapon. All our courses, site visits, and projects will invite reflection on how the examples of the city reflect aspects of the individual self (for good or ill). The program will focus on how the key to excellence for both empires and individuals lies within the relationship of the "I" to the "thou."
After discovering the just soul through the metaphor of the city, Plato turned around and used this good and just soul to make his own city great. We will encourage our participants to reflect on how they might leverage these lessons to make a difference within their own communities, organizations, and congregations.

This interdisciplinary program offers an in-depth exploration of Britain's contributions to scientific discovery, social policy, and human health. Students will walk in the footsteps of Darwin on the famous Sandwalk and observe, firsthand, the historic places where the discovery of the structure of DNA took place.. Excursions to the Scottish Highlands and Northern Ireland will combine outdoor adventure with reflections on the relationships between the natural world, health, and environmental stewardship. The program will be most appealing to students who enjoy being active outdoors (or want to begin doing so) and are passionate about combining science, policy, and spiritual insights to improve the world around them.

name: BYU London Centre Winter
text:
BYU London Centre Winter -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: European Soundscapes: Music, Literature, and Culture in London, Paris, and Croatia.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Win 2027 | 5 Jan–12 Apr | $12,900–13,400.
European Soundscapes: Music, Literature, and Culture in London, Paris, and Croatia
This study abroad program will focus on the relationship between culture, music, and literature through the lens of sound studies. We’ll start with the idea that sound is both an acoustic phenomenon and a means by which we understand and experience the world—the people we meet, the art we experience (whether visual, musical, literary, etc.), and the spaces and places we move through. London will serve as a focal point for this study, a focus supported by its historic place within both British musical and literary history, and its related role in global cultural interaction.
As students fulfill a variety of GE requirements, they will explore questions such as these: How does sound relate to cultural and artistic expression? Can the sounds of a city or natural space denote its musical and cultural history? Can an awareness of different sound environments expand one’s appreciation of different types of music? How do the spaces and geographical locations in which music is performed influence its reception and adaptation? Can a work of literature be noisy or quiet, melodious or cacophonous? How does reading and adapting literature with an awareness of sound and silence relate to aural memory, cultural identity, audience reception, authorial composition, narrative structure, or interpretation?
Students will read a wide variety of literature, study visual art on location in museums in London and elsewhere, and attend musical performances from a range of global cultures and in a variety of performance settings and venues. Aligning with coursework, students will take excursions to sites in both the UK and Europe, including Paris, Croatia, Cornwall, and Canterbury. As they study, students will explore the sonic environments and histories of London and other cities and places and consider their own engagement with the sonic in their daily experiences.

name: International Hydro-Engineering
text:
International Hydro-Engineering -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: International Challenges In Water Resources.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 26 Apr–6 May 2027 | $2,600–2,900.
International Challenges In Water Resources
Students will become partners with fellow BYU undergraduate and graduate students, as well as engineers from our partnering national hydrologic services (equivalent to USGS from the US) from different Central America/Caribbean countries, in applying water resources models methods and application development to critical problems faced by their country. This coming year we plan to help them generally with the integration of the Group on Earth Observations Global Water Sustainability (GEOGLOWS) hydrologic data into their decision making. We will be working in close collaborations with the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) in implementing their Hydrologic Status and Outlook (HydroSOS) and Early Warning for All initiatives as general guidance for GEOGLOWS integration. You will also learn the social impact cycle as taught in BYU’s Ballard Center for Social Impact and using those principles help design and implement customized services for the country or countries you are assigned. Courses will focus on distance collaboration with international partners to develop an approach to GEOGLOWS implementation to satisfy specific challenges.
The objective of this program is to provide students with opportunities to expand on the technical foundation learned through traditional classroom experiences and curriculum to develop the skills that will be necessary to practice and compete in a global environment.

text:
Chemistry Across Europe: Science, History, & Culture -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 28 Apr–3 Jun | $7,600–8,100.
We will spend six weeks in Europe visiting sites of both scientific and cultural importance. In general, we will spend one week in a city, which will be our base, visiting important sites in that city as well as those in surrounding cities. Our plan is to start in London, England and then proceed to Leiden (between Amsterdam and The Hague), Netherlands; Bruges, Belgium; Paris, France; Bern, Switzerland; and Milan/Florence/Rome, Italy. Day trips will be taken to cities like Oxford, Pisa, Lauterbrunnen, and Venice. Some of our cultural visits will include the British Museum in London, the Louvre and Eiffel Tower in Paris, Anne Frank’s house in Amsterdam, and the cathedral in Milan. We will see some of the great universities and educational institutions of Europe, including Oxford and Cambridge. As we go between countries, we will experience different cultures and languages. We will be in northern, central, and southern Europe. We will be in countries that speak English, Dutch, French, German, and Italian. Each morning, a student will present a short (ca. 30-minute) lecture on the place(s) we will visit. These presentations will be prepared the semester before we travel. They will usually have a focus on the chemistry related to the venue(s) of the day. We recommend that students that participate in this study abroad have taken CHEM 101 or 105 or the equivalent.

name: Discovering Early America in Europe 2027
text:
Discovering Early America in Europe 2027 -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 28 Jun–1 Aug | $8,400–8,900.
Join a remarkable tour that will bring you to some of the most historic sites of Europe while you discover how they impacted early American history. In Spain, visit citadels that influenced colonization in the Americas. Celebrate US Independence Day with the little town of Macharaviaya, which commemorates each July 4 with a Revolutionary War battle reenactment. Explore the mighty Rock of Gibraltar as you wind through tunnels built by the British during the largest battle of the American Revolution—fought 3,000 miles away from the United States! Skip over to Italy to discover the ancient foundations of American constitutionalism and government. Jaunt through southern France and walk in the footsteps of Thomas Jefferson as he visited ancient sites of the Roman Empire that inspired him. Jump to Switzerland and experience the majestic Swiss Alps as you learn about American religion and political thought in the heart of the Protestant Reformation. Continue to Paris, France, and discover how the French Revolution influenced early US politics as you visit the breathtaking Palace of Versailles, the sobering cells of the Conciergerie, and the Louvre Museum. Cross the English Channel to England and visit castles, palaces, and cathedrals that influenced America’s constitutional and political systems.

name: Eastern Europe Business
text:
Eastern Europe Business -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 8 May–19 Jun | $9,300–9,700.
FINLAND, ESTONIA, LATVIA, POLAND, GERMANY, CZECHIA, AUSTRIA, HUNGARY, SLOVENIA, CROATIA, BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA, MONTENEGRO, ALBANIA, GREECE
Featured cities: Helsinki, Kraków, Berlin, Prague, Vienna, Budapest, Dubrovnik, Athens, Santorini
When the Berlin Wall fell in 1989, countries across Eastern Europe faced the difficult task of reforming centrally planned economies and building new market institutions. Each country made different choices, with varying results. Over six weeks, we will travel through fourteen countries to explore how those choices shaped the region's economies, businesses, and communities. Before we leave, we will read and debate the promises and perils of capitalism.
Our route runs from Helsinki to Athens. We will stand at the Berlin Wall, visit Auschwitz-Birkenau, and see the KGB headquarters in Riga, the Stasi prison in Berlin, the Museum of Communism in Prague, and Albania's Cold War bunkers. These are the places where the old system is easiest to see. text:

Embark on a transformative journey through Ecuador’s Amazon, cloud forests, and high Andes while you get your GEs. This immersive program offers a unique opportunity to engage with the rich cultural traditions of the Quichua and Waorani peoples. In collaboration with local communities and several field schools, you’ll gain hands-on experience in sustainable development, cultural practices, linguistics, and biodiversity conservation. This program will explore some of the most spectacular gardens, landscapes, and vistas in Europe. This study abroad experience combines academic learning with adventure as we journey from the gorgeous flower shows of the Netherlands to the mountains of Wales and Scotland. Whether you're passionate about plants, ecology, outdoor recreation, history, literature, or travel, this program offers a unique opportunity to experience the benefits of nature firsthand.
Discover destinations including the Amsterdam Tulip Festival, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew, and the Chelsea Flower Show. Explore magnificent castle grounds, historic estates, and celebrated gardens while learning how landscape design reflects culture, history, and ecology. Along the way, study native ecosystems, medicinal plants, and the powerful connection between people and the natural world.
Experience Scotland's famous Jacobite Steam Train, inspiration for the Hogwarts Express, and visit the Isle of May, home to thriving seabird colonies and thousands of puffins. From iconic landscapes to unforgettable cultural experiences, this study abroad program offers a once-in-a-lifetime journey through some of Europe's most beautiful and inspiring destinations.

name: English Language in British Isles
text:
English Language in British Isles -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 21 Jun–30 Jul (approx.) | $9,300–9,800.
The English Language in British Isles program is a hands-on, experiential investigation into the origins and diversity of the English language. On this trip, we will take you to England, Scotland, Ireland, Wales, and Northern Ireland in the only study abroad program to visit all of the British Isles. In our travels, we will experience the diverse dialects of the British Isles from the received pronunciation in London, to the brogue in Scotland, to the Celtic lilt in Ireland and Wales. Along the way, we’ll teach you about the historical development of English and the important features that distinguish English dialects. Churches, fortresses, homes, and burial sites will reveal changes in the English language over the last 1,600 years.
Additionally, we will be investigating how books were developed and published in the British Isles, from the illuminated manuscripts of the Book of Kells, to early English editions of the Bible and through the early development of printing, to the modern publishing powerhouses in London and Edinburgh. During the experience, we will visit major sites in London, such as the Tower of London, Westminster Abbey, the Globe Theater, and St. Paul’s Cathedral. As we travel outside of London, we will see castles and cathedrals, publishing houses, world heritage and church history sites, along with the stunning countryside of the British Isles.

text:
English Language Teaching in Thailand -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 22 Jun–6 Aug | $4,900–5,400.
Teach English to college students while surrounded by an amazing culture, breathtaking scenery, and incredible food. Students will be visiting instructors at Ubon Ratchathani University (UBU). You will work in small groups to prepare English lesson plans, activities, and assessments for two hours of ESL instruction a day Monday–Thursday for motivated university students and will observe additional classmate instruction. BYU students will receive direct support in all teaching endeavors and will emerge as competent English language instructors capable of creating lesson plans on nearly any topic (not just English) which will serve them in any career or life situation involving teaching, whether that’s a classroom, a boardroom, a living room or a C-suite. Students will complete six credit hours of TESOL courses, which make up one-third of all coursework needed for a professional TESOL certificate (offered through BYU) that qualifies individuals to teach English all over the world.
Throughout the experience, we will visit regional and national areas of interest to better understand cultural perspectives on learning and knowledge. This includes a trip to Chiang Mai for a jungle hike, an elephant preserve, cooking classes, and sticky waterfalls. We’ll also visit a forest monastery, a unique glow-in-the-dark temple, and the world’s largest Buddhist candle celebration. We will tour other English language programs in the area, visit famous night markets, and feed giant turtles and hippos in the Ubon Ratchathani zoo. Students will also have opportunities for additional local exploration on many weeknights and some weekends. Undergraduates (and graduates) from any department are encouraged to apply. Previous experience teaching English as a second language is a plus but not necessary. No knowledge of the Thai language is necessary.

text:
Entrepreneurship in Hong Kong -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 23 Apr–14 Jun | $7,500–7,900.
HONG KONG, CHINA, VIETNAM
Learn to discover a need and launch a startup in one of the world’s most dynamic entrepreneurial ecosystems.
Hong Kong is one of the world's most dynamic startup and innovation hubs. It is a city where East meets West, colonial history meets cutting-edge finance, and street-level hustle meets world-class research universities. This study abroad program immerses students directly in that ecosystem, engaging with student entrepreneurs from Hong Kong universities to explore what it takes to build a venture in one of Asia's most competitive markets. You will move through the same process used by successful founders: discovering customer problems, testing ideas, validating demand, building prototypes, and launching a real venture.
We will spend a week each in Guangzhou, China and Hanoi, Vietnam, but the focus will be Hong Kong. This isn't a five-day sightseeing trip. This is five weeks of living in Hong Kong. Beyond the classroom and your startup business, you'll go deep into the city's neighborhoods through custom-designed cultural trails built around local food, customs, and history that push past the typical Instagram stops to discover the identity of a city and a people defined by change. You'll develop something most travelers never do: a real practice for how to enter a new city and culture. You will learn how to build local knowledge and design a genuine life of interaction with a place, not just a highlight reel of it.

name: Europe Civil and Construction Management Infrastructure Leadership
text:
Europe Civil and Construction Management Infrastructure Leadership -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: ITALY, FRANCE, SWITZERLAND, NETHERLANDS.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 14 May–4 Jun | $6,400–6,800.
ITALY, FRANCE, SWITZERLAND, NETHERLANDS
Join us for an unforgettable experience as we tour ancient and modern civil engineering projects in some of the most beautiful and culturally rich locations in Europe. After once-per-week meetings in the winter semester and three weeks of classroom study and preparatory work in the spring term, we will spend three weeks visiting sites in Italy, France, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. Site visits will likely include the Duomo and Accademia Gallery in Florence; the canals and Saint Mark’s Square of Venice; the Roman Arena in Verona; the old town of Geneva; the Eiffel Tower, the Versailles Palace, the Paris Metro in Paris; the Anne Frank house, various windmills, turbines, and water control structures in the Netherlands; as well as the TGV hi-speed rail system, various museums, and more!
Students will be organized into teams to study the technical features and construction associated with these sites and learn how ancient and modern civil engineers and construction and facility managers use creative methods to design and construct infrastructure that benefits society and fuels advancements in civilization. The course will be focused on all disciplines of civil and construction engineering: structures, transportation, construction and facilities management, geotechnical, water resources, and environmental. The course will include credit for the required civil and construction engineering course CCE 102—Sustainable Infrastructure. The course is open to Civil Engineering and Construction and Facilities Management majors only.

name: Europe: Global Perspectives on Energy and the Environment
text:
Europe: Global Perspectives on Energy and the Environment -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: ITALY, DENMARK, SLOVENIA, CROATIA.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 27 Apr–17 May | $6,900–7,200.
ITALY, DENMARK, SLOVENIA, CROATIA
Join us for a remarkable instructive experience as we learn about the current transformation that is occurring in the world’s electrical energy system and the future of sustainable energy. We will visit four countries in Europe: Denmark, Italy and Slovenia/Croatia. In Denmark, where more than 60% of the country’s electrical demand is generated from wind, we will see the largest wind turbines that have yet been built, climb the nacelle of a wind turbine, and tour related fabrication and testing facilities. In Italy we will tour a waste incineration plant that generates electricity, a solar PV cell fabrication facility, the largest pumped hydro-storage facility in the world and other sites focused on energy production and storage. We will also see up close the glacial retreat that has occurred due to climate change. In Slovenia/Croatia, we will visit a nuclear power plant and an electric vehicle production facility.
In each country, we will hear from local experts highlighting how renewable energy fits into the country’s energy portfolio. We will also be exposed to the rich cultural heritage and unique geography of each country, visiting sites of interest and sampling traditional local cuisine. A seminar series during the second block of winter semester will expose students to world energy reserves, environmental considerations related to energy production and use, the importance of government energy policy, and total economic and thermodynamic analysis of energy-producing methods. Prior to departing for Europe, we will also visit several regional energy-related sites, including coal, geothermal, hydroelectric, and natural gas-powered plants.
Over the course of the program, we will visit more than 20 different energy-related sites. The course will provide three credits of engineering technical elective toward graduation. The course is open to all majors, but preference will be given to engineering students who have taken an introductory Thermodynamics course. Students can take this class in the winter semester 2027 if they haven’t already done so.

name: Exercise & Medicine in Greece & Rome
text:
Exercise & Medicine in Greece & Rome -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 11 May–12 Jun | $TBA.
Come experience the birthplace of modern medicine, walking in the footsteps of Hippocrates and Galen. Shadow English-speaking physicians in Thessaloniki and visit ancient healing sites in Epidaurus and Rome. Discover how an active lifestyle can promote lifelong health by hiking to cliffside monasteries, kayaking in Crete, riding horses on Hydra, and swimming in the Aegean. In addition, we’ll engage with the New Testament, pausing to reflect at many of the apostle Paul’s stops. This comprehensive and immersive study abroad mirrors the holistic medicine that was discovered in Ancient Greece and Rome, where early physicians explored the healing power of medications but also of physical activity, social interaction, and spirituality. In this program, you will earn credits for EXSC 360 (Exercise is Medicine) as well as EXSC 399R (Internship), gain 50+ hours of medical shadowing which may be applicable toward medical school applications, and receive hands-on training prescribing, performing, and measuring different types of exercise in iconic Greek locations.

name: Exploring Our British Heritage
text:
Exploring Our British Heritage -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 13 Jul–13 Aug | $6,600–7,100.
Experience nineteenth-century Great Britain, the world in which thousands of our ancestors converted to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. This study abroad will explore the historical geography of England, Wales, and Scotland during the Industrial Revolution, as well as the British Mission that found great success in building the Church here. Each student will have the opportunity to guide the group through the life of a British convert or missionary (preferably, one of your own ancestors) with a firsthand experience of the historical and modern landscape of his or her community. For students with British ancestry (not required), this study will forge an especially strong connection to your own religious heritage.
Students will place these personal experiences in the broader context of heritage tourism as an aspect of economic development in modern British communities and as a form of pilgrimage for modern Church members. We will also study the geography of the Church in Great Britain in the context of the geography of other denominations. Therefore, our travels will focus on regions where the early Church was most concentrated: London, South Wales, the West Midlands, Northumberland, and Scotland.
Click here
to apply today!
Courses:
Students will enroll in 6 credits from the following courses while on this program:
GEOG 353—Heritage and Cultural Tourism (3 credit hours)
While we are being tourists of a sort, we will explore how British communities have preserved historical sites, how they present them to modern visitors, and the impact of these visitors on local economies.
GEOG 493R—Special Problems, “Geography of Religion” (3 credit hours)
As we visit sites important to the history of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and of other religions, we will learn how religious practice affects the human and natural landscape, and how location impacts religion.
Neither course has prerequisites, and both are open to all majors. Students may not take any other courses on this program, including BYU Online courses, without approval by the program director and ISP.

From couture fashion houses in Paris and Savile Row tailoring in London to wool production in Scotland, Renaissance craftsmanship in Italy, and modern design in Barcelona and Berlin, students will explore how culture, history, interior design, architecture, and craftsmanship influence the world of fashion and design.

name: Fashion, Food & the Finer Things in Paris & London
text:
Fashion, Food & the Finer Things in Paris & London -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 22 Jun–6 Aug | $6,900–7,600.
Come discover fashion, food, and the finer things in Paris and London! This program will explore the multicultural and aesthetic richness of these European capitals. Our curriculum will help you develop a deeper understanding of the French and British luxury industries while also acquainting you with the sometimes-seamy history of beautiful objects. The cities and some of their marquee monuments—the Musée du Chocolat, the Musée d’Orsay, the Palais Galliera, the Victoria & Albert Fashion Gallery, the Fashion & Textile Museum, and the Imperial War Museum, among others—will be our classroom. We will trace the evolution of the fashion industry from the specialty boutique to the department store and from the farthingale to fast fashion. This will include deep dives into the operations of Harrods, Liberty of London, Galeries Lafayette, Dior, and Louis Vuitton. We will venture beyond the berets and baguettes of postcard Paris to explore the multiethnic heritage of the city’s fashion, food, and art. In London, we will pay special attention to the transformation of fashion from private object to public display. Of particular interest to our program will be the cultural legacies of France’s and England’s colonial past. Our itinerary will also include excursions to the cities of La Rochelle, Bordeaux, Bayonne, Verdun, Bath, and Oxford.

name: From Mountains to Seas
text:
From Mountains to Seas -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: NEPAL, THAILAND, VIETNAM.
Term and cost: Field School Spr 2027 | 25 Apr–27 May | $11,200–11,600.
NEPAL, THAILAND, VIETNAM
EXPERIENCE DESIGN & MANAGEMENT (ExDM)
Join a four-week study abroad in Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam exploring how guides and instructors shape educational travel experiences. From an extended trek through the Himalayan mountains to cultural, outdoor, and guided experiences throughout Southeast Asia, students will explore principles of positive psychology and examine the behaviors that foster awe, savoring, and other positive outcomes through the lens of experience value. Students will serve as both participants and research assistants, observing and evaluating how guides structure experiences across challenging, aesthetic, and cultural settings. Using experience value and the theory of structured experience to guide our work, we will identify characteristics of effective guiding and examine how they elevate awe, savoring, and overall experience value. Our goal is to develop research that can be presented and published in academic settings.

name: Galápagos and Ecuador: Biodiversity and Evolution
text:
Galápagos and Ecuador: Biodiversity and Evolution -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: Come experience biodiversity and evolution in one of the world’s most extraordinary natural laboratories..
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 6–20 Aug (approx.) | $4,400–4,900.
Join us for an unforgettable journey from the high Andes of mainland Ecuador to the remarkable Galápagos Islands, where some of the world’s most extraordinary biodiversity provides a living laboratory for studying ecology and evolution. Explore historic Quito, stand at the equator at Mitad del Mundo, and venture into an Andean cloud forest alive with hummingbirds and hundreds of species of birds.
Then travel to the Galápagos and experience the landscapes and wildlife that helped transform our understanding of life on Earth. Visit the Charles Darwin Research Station, encounter giant tortoises in the Santa Cruz highlands, explore cactus forests and coastal ecosystems at Tortuga Bay, and hike the volcanic landscape of Sierra Negra. Snorkel the waters of Los Túneles, La Lobería, Cerro Tijeretas, and Kicker Rock while experiencing the remarkable connections between the islands’ terrestrial and marine ecosystems.
As we travel from mainland Ecuador to Santa Cruz, Isabela, and San Cristóbal, we will examine how geology, geography, isolation, and adaptation shape biodiversity. Students will compare continental and island ecosystems, explore the processes that generate unique species and communities, and consider the challenges of conserving these remarkable places.
Come experience biodiversity and evolution in one of the world’s most extraordinary natural laboratories.

text:

Location: GREECE, GHANA, AND THE NETHERLANDS.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 7 May–28 May | $4,200–4,600.
GREECE, GHANA, AND THE NETHERLANDS
This Accounting study abroad takes you across three countries—Greece, Ghana, and the Netherlands—focused around one theme: education and self-reliance. We will also focus on how faith strengthens both, and how faith sustains us through challenge and hardship. You will lead self-reliance firesides and visit BYU–Pathway Worldwide accounting students in Accra. Along the way, you will study the roots of Western learning and Christianity in Athens; worship with local members and visit the Accra Ghana Temple; experience natural wonders in Ghana; and trace the history of faith, business, and conscience, from the Cape Coast slave castles to the Anne Frank House to the Peace Palace at The Hague. name: Global Communications
text:
Global Communications -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 18 May–28 Jun | $7200-$7600.
Experience public relations and advertising in England and France, global centers of media and communication. Meet public relations and advertising professionals helping global organizations build brands, navigate cultures, and connect with people across borders. Walk the streets where abolitionists and women’s suffrage campaigners built social movements that changed society and discover what their legacy can teach us about using strategic communication for social good today.
Along the way, explore some of Europe’s most iconic places and consider what makes an experience memorable. Walk the grounds of Windsor Castle and Versailles, and experience landmarks such as the Tower of London. Study how history, storytelling, design, and symbolism work together to create distinctive identities and consider what today’s brands can learn from places that have captured the imagination for generations. The journey concludes on the French Riviera at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, where you’ll engage with some of the world’s most innovative strategic communications work and learn from the people creating it.
See Europe. Meet remarkable communicators. Study how brands and movements change minds. Come home seeing public relations and advertising differently.

name: Thailand Global Health
text:
Thailand Global Health -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Internship Spr–Sum 2027 | 7 May–3 Aug (approx.) | BYU Tuition.
Indorama Ventures have invited a BYU student to intern with Environmental/Occupational Health (EOH) managers for Indorama.This internship is part of a long-standing internship program that Indorama Ventures offers to students from around the world studying sustainability, accounting and finance, marketing, and investor relations.
The student intern will work directly with EOH professionals focusing on classic industrial hygiene issues at a global chemical manufacturing company using cutting-edge equipment and technology. The student will conduct all aspects of anticipation, recognition, evaluation, and control of workplace hazards. The student will also be involved in cultural activities that the company does on a regular basis.
The student intern will work with the Joint Action Committee of employees to ensure that all levels of our workforce are in statutory compliance, taking account of compulsory and periodic Health & Safety Training while equipping all staff with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) in line with their responsibilities. The intern will assist all EOH functions to maintain zero fatalities in the operations and to continually improve the performance in health, safety, and well-being through certification of the ISO 45001/OSHAS 18001 management system, internal corporate standards.
The internship commitment is a minimum of two months, but not more than three months.

Central and South America
: Gain valuable experience in a legal externship with firms and organizations located in such cities as Mexico City, Mexico; Asunción, Paraguay; and São Paulo, Brazil while learning about international transactions and corporate law during a semester abroad. : As an important region of international transactions and human rights organizations, externships in cities like Seoul, Korea and Tokyo, Japan offer meaningful opportunities for BYU law students to achieve a global perspective of legal topics. Learn about international business transactions and public international law from experts at BYU and be mentored by your externship provider, while living in a beautiful international city for a semester.

text:

Global Law Seminar:
Spend a semester living and working in leading centers of global commerce, finance, and law. The Global Law Seminar places students in externships with law firms, corporate legal departments, government agencies, and nongovernmental organizations where international legal issues are part of everyday practice. By studying and working alongside experienced attorneys, you'll gain firsthand insight into how law facilitates cross-border transactions, supports global markets, and shapes international governance.
A Global Perspective on Law:
The Global Law Seminar is more than a study abroad experience. It is an opportunity to learn law where global economic activity and international legal institutions converge. Students return with practical legal experience, stronger professional judgment, greater cross-cultural competence, and a deeper understanding of how American law fits within an increasingly interconnected world.
Global Legal Centers
London, England
One of the world's premier financial and legal capitals, London offers opportunities to work with international law firms, barristers' chambers, financial institutions, government agencies, and organizations engaged in cross-border transactions, dispute resolution, and commercial law.
Geneva, Switzerland
Home to the United Nations and numerous international organizations, Geneva is a leading center for public international law, international trade, investment governance, diplomacy, and multilateral dispute resolution.
Seoul, South Korea
As a global hub for technology, manufacturing, and international commerce, Seoul offers experience with the legal challenges surrounding multinational business, intellectual property, cross-border investment, and global supply chains.
Tokyo, Japan
Tokyo is one of the world's leading financial and commercial centers, where students gain insight into international business transactions, corporate law, finance, and comparative legal practice in one of Asia's most influential economies.
São Paulo, Brazil
Brazil's financial and corporate capital, São Paulo is a center for corporate governance, capital markets, regulatory compliance, and international business throughout Latin America.
Mexico City, Mexico
A major center for trade, finance, and international commerce, Mexico City provides opportunities to engage with legal issues involving cross-border business, investment, immigration, and regional economic integration.
Additional Locations
The Global Law Seminar also offers placements in other strategically important cities where legal, commercial, and institutional factors create distinctive opportunities for professional growth and comparative legal study.

text:
Italy and Greece: Rhetoric, Architecture, and Food -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: ITALY AND GREECE.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 12 May–16 Jun | $7,200–7,600.
ITALY AND GREECE
STUDY ABROAD GENERAL EDUCATION (SAGE)
From the ancient city to the kitchen, “Rhetoric, Architecture, and Food” investigates how the preparation of meals, the production of public spaces, and the art of persuasion all helped to shape the classical world. Study during your spring term in Athens and Rome, with on-site lectures that give plenty of time to savor the city without the summertime press of tourists. Good itineraries to Greece and Italy normally hit the highlights, but this exceptional program allows time for exploring and visiting (and revisiting) well beyond the trodden paths—and without the noisy crowds. Did we mention the architecture, the pasta . . . the gelato?
The academic goals of this program focus on General Education curriculum, drawing on the incredible breadth of the Greco-Roman classroom. We will start in Athens, travel through the island of Santorini, Sicily, Capri, the Amalfi Coast, Rome, Florence, and end the semester in Venice. Enjoy Europe’s springtime—without the oppressive heat and crowds that fill the city and its museums later in the year.

The program begins with a month-long immersive residency in

memorials in Hiroshima and Nagasaki

Japan Study Abroad 2 (Summer Term 2027)
will travel across

, experiencing the distinct cultures, landscapes, and traditions of

and
Fukuoka,
Koka’s ninja
sites,

Tokushima
and
Nagoya, Ghibli
-themed attractions, and other remarkable historical and cultural landmarks along the way. We will also explore Kamakura’s iconic

the
coastal beaches of Enoshima,
and sweeping views of
Mt. Fuji.
Along the way, we will enjoy traditional arts and performances and spend time in
Tokyo,
Japan’s vibrant capital and a hub of modern culture, before continuing on to
Tokyo DisneySea
and concluding in
Sendai

This student exchange program in Korea provides students an opportunity to attend Kyung Hee University in Suwon, just south of Seoul. Since its founding in 1949, the university has grown to become one of the largest in Korea; our program is based at the Suwon campus. Striving to bridge cultural and social gaps, Kyung Hee University has a commitment to internationalization, academic excellence, and research that has defined it as one of the top educational institutions in Korea.

name: Landscapes and Nations of Europe
text:
Landscapes and Nations of Europe -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 15 May–13 Jun | $6,900–7,400.
This geographical journey through Western Europe will visit ten countries (Italy, Croatia, Slovenia, Hungary, Austria, Slovakia, Czechia, Germany, Denmark, and Sweden) to study the natural and built landscapes of Europe and to better understand historic and contemporary issues stemming from nations and nationalism. We will consider political, cultural, linguistic, and religious influences in the formation of nation-states, the aspirations of separatist regions, the impact of immigrants and minorities on national identity, and the role of post-nationalism as represented by the European Union. Along our way we will meet with folks from all walks of life to better understand their experiences living in the dynamic political landscape of Europe. Additionally, we will hike, bike, walk, and ride through many other geographical landscapes: urban and rural, agrarian and industrial, religious and secular, mountain and shore. We will wander around the ancient Forum and hike the Appian Way in Rome, climb to the best view of the Florence Duomo, ride a gondola in Venice, bask in thermal waters in Budapest, hike around Lake Bled in the Julian Alps, visit Frauenkirche is Dresden, swim in the Danube and bike along its banks, cross the Oresund Strait, walk near the old Berlin Wall, visit the mermaid in Copenhagen Harbor, identify ethnic separatism and competition in the landscape today, and witness the memorials and troubling histories of ethnic genocides of the past. In sum, we will visit a range of castles, cathedrals, restaurants, farms, mountains, plains, hills, coastlines, museums, monuments, headquarters, and neighborhoods to learn how to "read" both the iconic and vernacular European landscapes. Students will also have free time to do their own explorations of iconic cites like Rome, Florence, Venice, Vienna, Budapest, Prague, Berlin, and Copenhagen.

name: Morocco
text:
Morocco -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Field School Spr–Sum 2027 | 7 May–10 Jul | $4,500–5,000.
Morocco is rich in complexity and anthropologists have long researched, theorized, and written about the people who traverse, work, claim, contest, negotiate, barter, marry, worship, migrate from and return to this place. This ethnographic field school will be in Fez Morocco, a 1200-year-old city that has experienced intense urban change. Students will receive training in anthropology research methods and collaborate with Moroccan university students to identify and ethnographically research a social, political, cultural or environmental issue. Potential topics include gender, social customs and rituals; education, sufism and spirituality; medicine and magic; multispecies relations; as well as youth and social movements. Students will spend two weeks contextualizing Fez by traveling around Morocco (a week in the south, and a weekend in the north), and 7 weeks embedding themselves into a social context and collecting ethnographic data collaboratively in Fez. Students will also be introduced to historical and ethnographic studies of Morocco and attend guest lectures from scholars who do fieldwork in Morocco, focusing on anthropological representations of peoples, places, phenomena. We will discuss how scholars have captured life in Moroccan communities and how the process of describing “Moroccans” and “Maghariba” (North Africans) contributes to anthropological theories of personhood, identity, gender, religion, illness, politics and economics.

text:
Nepal Global Health -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Internship Spr 2027 | 24 Apr–23 May | $TBD.
Often called the “rooftop of the world,” Nepal is home to deeply rooted Hindu and Buddhist traditions, rich in iconography and spiritual significance. The Kathmandu Valley alone contains seven UNESCO World Heritage sites that beautifully intertwine both religious legacies. Amid this cultural depth, students will gain firsthand experience exploring public health challenges and opportunities within communities throughout Nepal.
Working alongside local and international partners, student interns will engage with a variety of public health professionals, healthcare providers, community organizations, and populations. Depending on their placement and the needs of local partners, students will explore a range of public health issues, including occupational and environmental health, maternal and child health, community health, health education, and healthcare delivery.
Experiences may include fieldwork examining occupational hazards and their effects on workers, families, and surrounding communities; collaborating with hospitals and local public health workers; developing and teaching health education; and supporting community-based health initiatives. Students may also engage with schools, children’s homes, local physicians, healthcare facilities, and other community organizations.
This program is designed for self-starter student interns who are eager to learn through meaningful engagement with Nepali partners. Students will be encouraged to take initiative, adapt to the needs of their placements, and gain a broader understanding of how culture, environment, occupation, family, and access to healthcare influence individual and community health. The internship also includes a four-day trek through the Annapurna region, offering students the opportunity to experience Nepal’s breathtaking landscapes, mountain culture, and natural beauty up close.

text:
Nepal: Trekking, Water, & Geology in the Himalayas -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 10–31 May | $TBD.
Trek through the Himalayas of Nepal while you earn your physical science GE or a geology elective. On a ten-day trek through the Annapurna region, you'll study water at its source, in the mountains that supply rivers for more than a billion people downstream. Glaciers, snowmelt, groundwater, and monsoon rains feed steep rivers that support villages and hydropower projects, and along the trail you'll trace the entire water cycle with your own eyes, feet, and field notebook. Working alongside faculty and local guides, you'll learn to read a landscape closely and ask the questions that matter everywhere: Where does water come from? Who gets it, and who decides? How do mountains, climate, and rivers shape the communities that depend on them? Through field observation, stream and spring measurements, and conversations with Nepali communities living with floods, drought, and a changing climate, you'll examine water scarcity, dams and diversions, water quality, and shared rivers, then carry those lessons home to the American West. We will also participate in several days of service in remote villages as they recover from recent devastating floods. No science background is required, just a willingness to walk, look closely, and think about your own role as a steward of the water that sustains life on Earth.

How did the discovery of new worlds reshape Europe?
This GE study abroad program explores how encounters with new peoples, ideas, and environments transformed European culture, science, and society from the age of exploration through the modern era. Through literature, art, history, and postcolonial theory, students will examine the cultural legacies of empire, race, migration, and national identity, while considering how Europe was shaped not only by its colonies, but also by the peoples and cultures it encountered around the globe.
At the same time, students will investigate the history of science in the Netherlands, Belgium, and France through museums, monuments, historic sites, and hands-on field experiences. Using these places as a living classroom, we will explore how developments in navigation, astronomy, chemistry, engineering, and environmental science influenced the rise of modern Europe and were themselves shaped by broader cultural, political, and ethical debates. Based primarily in Amsterdam, the program also includes extended travel throughout Belgium and France.

name: Paris: United Frances
text:
Paris: United Frances -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Fall 2027 | 16 Sep–13 Dec | $TBD.
“La France” evokes what is beautiful, timelessly
romantique
, and “praiseworthy,” with some perplexities in between. Thinking in terms of “United Frances” is not about imitating a younger nation; this study abroad program intends rather to take students to see this fact: "La France," singular, does not exist outside of the many regions and territories added up over the centuries, through alliances or colonial conquests, and consolidated into one indivisible nation. That is, "indivisible" with a few revolutions and independences, like the one from which Haiti emerged in 1804 that was eventually headed by an ex-slave who became general and governor, who died in a dungeon in France. Sounds epic, like the movie
Gladiator,
but it's true! Is it a fairy tale? You’ll see when you’re in the dungeon.
Students will see that not all French territories are the same: New Caledonia has the same status as Tahiti but not Brittany. All French citizens carry a French passport and have a social security number, but they are not all "French" in the same way. From Reims, where the idea of France traditionally began with the baptism of Clovis, to Lourdes in the Pyrenees, where a young woman saw the Virgin Mary, the country is traditionally Christian Catholic. But students will learn that there are more active Catholics in places like Vendée and Martinique than in Paris and its surrounding region, despite Victor Hugo’s Notre Dame cathedral. And there are a few Latter-day Saints throughout the country among the faithful Christians: Bordeaux is not only the wine country, it's also where a special witness of Jesus Christ was born and grew up. And what should we say about gastronomy—pastries, regional dishes, and more? You’ll taste and burn the calories!
Much of this program is about understanding La France in its plurality, as far as the Caribbean. But it will not be a sightseeing tour. It will be a once-in-a-lifetime learning experience with a Franco-Haitian professor of French and his French family as guides and language coaches. Sign up now! You won’t regret it—you’ll see!

name: Pasefika Alliance for Indigenous Research Internship
text:
Pasefika Alliance for Indigenous Research Internship -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Internship Sum 2027 | 21 Jul–4 Aug | $5,300–5,800.
The BYU Pasefika Alliance for Indigenous Research (PAIR) internship program is an immersive clinical, public health, and environmental research experience focused on understanding, addressing, and reducing Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) health disparities among Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander (NHPI) populations, while also exploring how Indigenous cultures understand illness and use traditional knowledge to manage their environments. The prevalence and incidence of ADRD within NHPI communities are not well understood due to the lack of comprehensive research. However, we do know that ADRD disproportionately affects low-income and minority populations, including NHPIs, who experience an earlier onset of Alzheimer's disease and more health-related risk factors.
Students involved in this program will actively participate in recruitment, enrollment, and data collection during our culturally tailored, hands-on Brain Health Fairs in Tonga. At these events, we provide vital ADRD education and collect essential data and biological samples, raising awareness and promoting good brain health within these communities. Students will work closely with our partners in Tonga to conduct these workshops in villages and church groups, focusing on participants aged fifty and above. In New Zealand, they will participate in a pilot study to understand how generations of local management has led to insights on the management of coastal ecosystems.
Finally, students will participate in genetic studies that help to better understand the genetic risks that may contribute to the high rates of ADRD throughout Polynesia. In all aspects of this program, students will interact with indigenous medical and educational professionals, as well as government and church leaders, to promote sustainable improvement in healthcare in Tonga and stewardship in Aotearoa New Zealand, leaving a lasting impact on the community.

This program will focus on the historical and applied aspects of microbiology and molecular biology. Students will visit London, Cambridge, Oxford, Amsterdam, Delft, Gouda, and Paris as part of their study abroad. Visits to museums will be highlighted with presentations that the public do not get to see, including disease diagnosis using London plague pit skeletons, Fleming’s lab where penicillin was discovered, microscopes made by van Leeuwenhoek and Darwin, and the Cavendish Laboratory! name: Threats to Democracy in Europe
text:
Threats to Democracy in Europe -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 18 Jun–21 Jul (approx.) | $7,700–8,200.
Throughout its history, Europe has been a continent of remarkable diversity. Differences in culture, ethnicity, religion, and political interests have often brought societies into conflict, culminating in the devastating wars of the twentieth century. In the aftermath of these conflicts, European countries increasingly embraced democracy and political integration in the hope of preventing history from repeating itself. For nearly six decades, democratic institutions and European integration fostered an unprecedented period of peace and cooperation, helping to bridge long-standing national and ethnic rivalries. Yet in recent years, these institutions have come under increasing strain, raising important questions about the future of democracy, security, and European unity. This study abroad program places students at the center of these debates. By exploring Europe's history, politics, and contemporary challenges firsthand, you will gain a deeper understanding of how the continent has evolved and where it may be headed. Along the way, you will develop the theoretical frameworks and analytical tools needed to make sense of Europe's past, interpret its present, and evaluate its future.

text:

Term and cost: Study Abroad Sum 2027 | 26 Jul–4 Aug | $3,400–3,900.
This program gives students a chance to study and learn from the Costa Rica public health system, specifically examining the Nicoya Peninsula Blue Zone. Students will be immersed in the local culture as they engage with residents and observe how public health programs, policies, systems, local culture and the environment contribute to the overall health of populations. Students will experience the impact of social factors and built environments on healthy behaviors in urban and rural areas and learn to identify how American values related to health differ from those in Costa Rica. They will study innovative approaches to tackling public health challenges and explore the important relationship between the natural environment and human health. Students will participate in active learning experiences and have many opportunities to be physically active. This study abroad will be most appealing to students that are passionate about health, enjoy leading an active lifestyle (or want to begin doing so), and desire to experience diverse cultures and their impact on health. A key element of this study abroad will invite students to explore the role of faith in healthy lifestyle choices and ways to build healthy communities (AKA “Blue Zones”).

Join us for an opportunity to learn about renewable energy while in Denmark and Norway, two countries with substantial renewable energy generation but with completely different resource bases. This study abroad includes a four-week course taught at several sites, including the Technical University of Denmark campus located in Copenhagen, Denmark (a widely acclaimed university with long history in technology) and Aalborg University in the Northern portion of peninsular Denmark called Jutland (ranked as the best engineering university in Europe several years in a row by major ranking organizations).

You will gain experience and exposure that can be applied to renewable energy development in the USA and globally. We will also visit Frederiksborg Castle, Kronborg Castle, and various Viking sites. You can experience firsthand how sustainable living practices have been adopted.

name: Rome & Vienna: National Identity and Belonging
text:
Rome & Vienna: National Identity and Belonging -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Fall 2027 | 13 Sep–7 Dec | $12,000–12,800.
With Rome and Vienna as home bases, students will experience how national identities are constructed and how we can become more actively engaged in building Christlike communities of belonging. In every sense, the cities will be our classroom: cooking classes in Naples, the birthplace of pizza; gondola rides in Venice; art museums in Florence; bike rides along the Danube beneath an 11th-century monastery; touring Jewish cemeteries in Prague; world-famous Christmas markets in Salzburg; and so much more as we immerse ourselves in the diverse cultures of Italy, Austria, Slovakia, and Czechia.
Through such immersive learning opportunities, we will learn about Italy’s and Austria’s imperial, national, and countercultural complexities. From Michelangelo to Klimt, Verdi to Mozart, Machiavelli to Freud, how could countries that have created some of the most globally celebrated artists, musicians, and intellectuals also give rise to the likes of Mussolini and Hitler? Somewhere between these extremes, Rome and Vienna represent a tangible richness of human resilience, reflection, and rediscovery. Surrounded by centuries of architectural, artistic, culinary, literary, musical, and sociopolitical expressions of national identity and belonging, our program will be centered on three core questions: How are national identities constructed? How do we create communities of belonging? How do we embrace the prophetic call to become peacemakers in an era of ever-increasing hostility?

name: Spain: Camino de Santiago
text:
Spain: Camino de Santiago -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: A DIALOGUE WITH NATURE, CULTURE, AND THE DIVINE.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 27 Apr–19 Jun | $7,900–8,400.
A DIALOGUE WITH NATURE, CULTURE, AND THE DIVINE
The Camino de Santiago crosses Spain along a path forged in the 11th century when the faithful walked to the place where the remains of the Apostle James the Elder (Santiago el Mayor) were believed to have been buried in northwestern Spain. Over the centuries, many pilgrims have worked their way across Europe to venerate the remains of the saint. Along the way, they shared stories, songs, architectural designs, religious feelings, and language, and for many it was on the Camino that the ideal of Christian identity and unity was solidified. Those who walk the Camino today experience an unparalleled sequence of historical, architectural, and artistic encounters that tell the story of Spain and of Europe. This study abroad will place your name alongside other pilgrims who have become part of the Camino legacy. More importantly, the Camino is a spiritual journey: a journey of self-discovery, of penance, of service, and of camaraderie. Modern-day pilgrims learn about themselves as they enter into the human conversation with others along the trail. Your interactions with other pilgrims along the way will teach you to appreciate and value the lives and experiences of those who are not of our faith or culture. The result is an increased love of God and humanity.
Prior to beginning our trek on the Camino, we will spend time in Barcelona visiting significant sites that will inform our cultural experience. We will also visit the
Monasterio Viejo de San Juan de la Peña
, built in the 10
th
century. The monastery played a significant role both in the development of the Camino as well as being the cradle of the Kingdom of Aragón. We will begin our nearly 475-mile trek along the
Camino Francés
in Roncesvalles in the Pyrenees and end in Santiago de Compostela in the western province of Galicia. On rest days, we will visit important cultural and spiritual sites, including the
Monasterios de Suso y Yuso
(the cradle of the Spanish language), the famed
Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Silos
, Oviedo, the
Iglesia de Santiago de Peñalba
and the
Valle de Silencio
. As you walk the Camino, you will collect
sellos
in your pilgrim’s
credenciales
. You will present these small booklets at the Pilgrims’ Office in Santiago de Compostela where you will receive your
Compostela
, the certificate awarded to you for completing the pilgrimage. At the end of the experience, we will travel to Finisterre (“end of the earth”), where early pilgrims often went to collect their seashell as evidence of the completion of their journey, and then to Muxia, another important pilgrimage site on the Atlantic Ocean.

Spend over 20 hours per week shadowing medical providers, observing multiple specialties, and gaining a broad perspective on public and global health. text:
Spain Spring -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 27 Apr–17 Jun | $7,600–8,000.
For millennia, Spain has stood at the crossroads of cultures and civilizations. Basques, Romans, Visigoths, Arabs, Jews, and many other peoples have left their mark on the Iberian Peninsula. Although five centuries of nation-building have repeatedly sought to forge its diverse ethnic and linguistic communities into a single national identity, Spain remains a fascinating mosaic of distinct cultures, traditions, and identities.
Participants in this program will experience this extraordinary heritage firsthand. For example, they will wander the medieval streets of Toledo, marvel at the soaring arches of Córdoba’s Mosque-Cathedral, trace the route of Pamplona’s famous running of the bulls, and stand beneath Segovia’s magnificent Roman aqueduct. They will encounter masterpieces by Velázquez, Goya, Picasso, and Dalí and discover the landscapes and cities that shaped the imaginations of some of the world’s most celebrated writers, such as Cervantes, Lope de Vega, and Santa Teresa de Jesús.
The Spain program is based in Alcalá de Henares, a UNESCO World Heritage city just outside Madrid. Home to a historic university and the birthplace of Miguel de Cervantes, Alcalá offers students a safe, welcoming, and culturally rich environment in which to experience daily life in Spain. Alcalá’s location also provides easy access to Madrid and its remarkable landmarks, including the Prado Museum, Retiro Park, and the Puerta del Sol.

name: Activity, Nutrition, Cuisine and Culture in Italy
text:
Activity, Nutrition, Cuisine and Culture in Italy -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: Please note this program is fast paced with significant physical activity.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 26 May–26 Jun 2027 | $8,200–8,700.
The Mediterranean lifestyle includes a dietary pattern and way of living unique to countries near the Mediterranean Sea and is associated with good health and prevention of chronic disease. Italy is central to the Mediterranean lifestyle and pattern of eating. Furthermore, Italy is rich with history, cuisine, agriculture, a diversity of physical features and terrains (e.g., coastal landforms, beaches, and mountains with stunning views), and opportunities for outdoor physical activity. These varieties create a unique setting for student learning and experience in physical activity, nutrition, cuisine, and culture. Therefore, the overall purpose of this study abroad program is to experience, compare, and contrast the activity/lifestyle, nutrition, cuisine, food environments, and cultures in rural and urban settings throughout Italy. This program includes visits to the following places in Italy: Rome (Lazio region), Civitella Afladena (Abruzzo region), Matera (Basilicata region), Amalfi Coast (Campania region), Pompeii (Campania region), Alpi Apuane Mountains (Tuscany region), Cinque Terre (Liguria region), Parma (Emilia-Romagna region), Venice (Veneto region), and several other small villages near these regions.
This unique program includes a combination of: 1) physical activities (hiking, walking), 2) discussions of nutrition and human health (e.g., Mediterranean lifestyle, physical activity biology, “Blue Zones,” the relationship between social interaction and health, human research studies in activity and nutrition, society and food, nutrient properties of Mediterranean foods, chronic disease, etc.), 3) food tours and local cuisine, 4) visits to food production sites, and 5) guided and self-guided tours to explore local culture. Specifically, this program includes visits to a lemon grove, dairy farm, chestnut mill, bakery, olive farm, parmesan cheese factory, and balsamic production site; guided tours of several museums; an academic lecture at the prestigious University of Padova; and eating and interacting with local residents and restaurant owners (e.g., fish production and preservation demonstration, pizza-making and bread-making and pasta-making workshops).
Please note this program is fast paced with significant physical activity
(including city walking/standing, significant mountain/hill hiking, a hike up a volcano (Vesuvius), and sea kayaking and swimming). This program may be of interest for students in Life Sciences (e.g. Nutrition, Dietetics, Food Science), pre-med or pre-health professions majors, and majors related to travel. All majors may apply.

text:

Prepare for a future in the mental health professions through BYU’s Therapy Approaches and Cultural Diversity Across Italy study abroad. Designed for undergraduate students exploring careers in marriage and family therapy, clinical psychology, social work, counseling, and related fields, this program introduces students to therapy fundamentals and approaches such as cognitive-behavioral, psychodynamic, and strategic therapy at renowned Italian clinical training centers. Led by BYU Marriage and Family Therapy faculty, alongside their spouses who are also practicing therapists, the program offers mentorship into how a career as a therapist can be built and sustained across different life stages and specialties.

name: Voices of Oceania: Listening and Storytelling in New Zealand and Australia
text:
Voices of Oceania: Listening and Storytelling in New Zealand and Australia -- BYU study abroad / international study program (Kennedy Center ISP).
Location: NEW ZEALAND AND AUSTRALIA.
Term and cost: Study Abroad Spr 2027 | 25 Apr–12 Jun | $13,200–13,600.
NEW ZEALAND AND AUSTRALIA
STUDY ABROAD GENERAL EDUCATION (SAGE)
Become a better listener and engaging storyteller as you spend seven weeks listening to and learning from Māori, Pacific Island, and Australian communities who use stories to transmit core values, sustain relationships, and connect people to place. We will be shepherded through New Zealand’s volcanic valleys and lush rainforests and through Australia’s iconic Outback and dazzling cities by local guides who have a deep understanding of the oral traditions and storytelling practices of Oceania’s diverse peoples.
You will also learn how to share your own story as you patter through Hobbiton, twitch through Kāpiti Island Nature Reserve to glimpse endangered birds, cruise across Fiordland National Park’s spectacular Milford Sound, trek through the oldest tropical rainforest on earth, stargaze the Southern Cross from the Australian Outback, and wander through Sydney’s lit-up streets during its annual festival of light, music, and food. Your increased capacity to tell your own story will help you find meaning in your incredible experience, making this a truly transformative study abroad program.
“Voices of Oceania” will be a physically active program, full of opportunities to explore the breathtaking landscapes of New Zealand and Australia. We will be floating beneath the glowworms of Waitomo Caves, swimming in the crystal-clear coastal bays of Abel Tasman National Park, sea-kayaking in Ōkārito Lagoon, hiking along wild stretches of the Tasman Sea coastline, snorkeling among the Great Barrier Reef’s coral gardens and 1,600 species of fish, and trailing an indigenous guide around Uluru. These awe-inspiring experiences in nature will deepen the community we create through sharing and listening to stories.
